hypothesis: Same build as exp-rayon-io, re-measured on the boxes as they are now. The boxes were idle-stopped and restarted (likely new physical hosts) between exp-rayon-io and the CPU-feature runs, whose c8g gains (~2.5%) did not stack. If this re-measure also lands near 6.55s on c8g, those gains were host change.
llm_commentary: First same-boot measurement on m9g.2xlarge (AWS Graviton5, Neoverse V3, 3.3 GHz, 32 GiB): stock main 6.46s [6.49/6.39/6.50] → champion 4.59s [4.61/4.64/4.52], -28.9%, the largest gain of the four families (c8a -14.2%, c8i -24.8%, c8g -25.6% on the same boots). Stock, Graviton5 sits between c8a (5.55s) and c8i (7.31s); with the four committed changes it becomes the fastest box and the cheapest per run ($0.00050 OD). The changes remove per-call locks, atomics and cross-thread wakeups (cursor open/close under the txn mutex, the settings RwLock, a keccak-cache lookup per SLOAD, tokio's blocking-pool mutex and condvar), the overhead that weighs most on the Graviton cores, while V3's wider core and larger caches then serve the remaining MDBX seeks and EVM work well. Next: the rest of the instance-configuration sweep with m9g included.
